key_insight: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization shows that rigid nozzles maximize impulse, while flexible nozzles deliver better energy efficiency in pulsed-jet propulsion.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a design rule for bioinspired underwater thrusters: use rigid geometries for peak thrust and flexible geometries when efficiency and maneuverability are the priority.
method: 3D fluid-structure interaction simulations of pulsed-jet nozzles
Multi-objective Bayesian optimization over nozzle geometry
Comparison of rigid vs. flexible nozzle deformation and jet performance
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 5× impulse amplification for rigid nozzles, about 2.5× for flexible nozzles, and a ~1.8× higher normalized impulse-to-energy ratio for flexible designs.
watch_item: The optimization appears simulation-based, so experimental validation and robustness to real-world fabrication/material variability remain important concerns.
paper_title: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization of rigid and flexible nozzles for energy-efficient pulsed jet propulsion
